images.title: Turns all around us
images.purpose: Show that lines and turns hide in everyday things, and the turn is what we want to name and measure.
images.composition: One open door seen from above, with a straight wall line and the door line, wide empty space around it.
images.exact_structure: Left: a straight grey #6B7280 horizontal line for the wall. From its right end, one teal #0072B2 line (the door) swings up at a slant, with a small reddish purple #CC79A7 curved arc between wall and door showing the turn. Right: one amber #E69F00 straight stick standing apart for contrast. Exactly 2 straight lines meeting at 1 point, 1 arc, 1 separate stick.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a speech bubble, person or background room scene
images.takeaway: A turn happens where two straight lines meet.
images.description: A grey wall line and a teal door line meeting at a point, with a purple arc showing the turn, and a separate amber straight stick.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the turn and say how much the door opened.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
